chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave the penalty of cutting (the hand) for an egg. I said: 'What is the egg?' He said: 'An egg worth a quarter of a dinar.' I said: 'That is the minimum threshold for the thief,' and he remained silent.

key_terms.رُبْعُ دِينَارٍ: A quarter of a dinar (a specific monetary value)
key_terms.قَطَعَ: To cut (specifically the hand as a legal punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for the punishment of cutting the hand in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the nisab (minimum value) for hadd al-sariqa as a quarter of a dinar, illustrating the practical application of this threshold by Imam Ali (AS) in the case of an egg. The Imam's silence upon the narrator's confirmation signifies his tacit approval of this specific valuation, which became a foundational reference in Shia jurisprudence for determining the eligibility of thieves for amputation.
